newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: TAP to seek partners after restructuring.
newsitem.headline: TAP to seek partners after restructuring.

text.p: Loss-making Portuguese state airline TAP-Air Portugal must conclude its restructuring plan before forming any strategic alliance with foreign airlines, a government minister said on Tuesday.
"The restructuring of TAP will be concluded soon, and only then should strategic alliances for the company be discussed," Planning and Public Works Minister Joao Cravinho told reporters.

In July 1994 the European Commission authorised a capital increase of 180 billion escudos ($1.2 billion) in government aid for TAP in stages as part of a restructuring plan which laid out financial targets to bring the airline back to profit by 1997.
TAP on Tuesday reported a net loss of 5.4 billion escudos ($35 million) in the first eight months of 1996, less than the 6.4 billion escudos ($41 million) loss targeted in the restructuring plan.
In January to August 1995 the airline posted a greater loss of 8.5 billion escudos ($55 million).
"TAP is recovering and generally its financial results are better," Cravinho said.
He said the airline's plans eventually to renew its fleet of medium-range aircraft should bring annual cost savings of 7.5 billion escudos ($49 million). ($1=154.4 escudos)
